segments.t: korTTY can collect KTPH000anonymous usage statisticsKTPH001 to help decide which features are worth improving and to find crashes and frequent errors. This is entirely optional and can be turned on or off at any time. On a first launch the checkbox in the master-password setup comes KTPH002pre-selectedKTPH003, so confirming that dialog as-is starts collection — clear it there, or switch it off later, and nothing is collected.

KTPH000Your decision, once.KTPH001 Nothing is collected before you confirm. You are asked once, together with the master-password setup on first launch, where the checkbox is pre-selected; existing installations are asked once after unlocking, with a dialog that counts every dismissal as "no".
KTPH000Anonymous.KTPH001 No account, no login, and no persistent device identifier is transmitted.
KTPH000Revocable.KTPH001 You can change your decision at any time under KTPH002Settings → PrivacyKTPH003. Turning it off stops collection immediately and discards any data that has not yet been sent.
app start, feature used (e.g. a tool opened, a backup created)
number of open terminal tabs, whether AI is enabled
a random number regenerated on every launch and after one hour of inactivity
The session ID is KTPH000notKTPH001 a persistent identifier: it is newly generated each time and cannot be traced back to you across launches.
A few terminal features report how they are used, with flags, coarse counts and fixed names only. Counts are rounded down to 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 or 20, so seven panes are reported as 5.
a row of the command palette runs
the kind of row (KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002 or KTPH003) and whether the search started with a scope prefix such as KTPH004 or KTPH005
a pane starts showing another highlighting rule set
a built-in set's id, or KTPH000 or KTPH001, and where the choice came from (menu, shortcut, connection or default)
you add panes to multi-exec, remove them or stop it
whether multi-exec is still on, and the rounded number of panes, tabs and windows taking part
the previous session is opened again
the Session Restore setting (KTPH000, KTPH001 or KTPH002), whether the menu, the startup bar or the automatic restore opened it, and the rounded number of windows and tabs

The search text, the names of commands, tabs, connections, snippets and rule sets, the patterns, and anything typed into the panes are never sent. Changes on the settings pages are reported as the name of the setting and, for switches and choices, the new value; for the quick-select letters and patterns and for rebound shortcuts only whether you changed them.
KTPH000InsertKTPH001 or KTPH002RunKTPH003 on a code block of an AI chat is used
KTPH000 or KTPH001, and whether it ended KTPH002, KTPH003 (the Run confirmation was declined) or KTPH004 (the policy, the block or the pane did not allow it)
The block, its language, the command, the pane, the tab, the host and the reason for a refusal are never sent.

When a program uses the KTPH001Control APIKTPH002, korTTY reports which methods are used and what kind of client used them. An AI assistant connected through KTPH000 is also reported by tool and by how the call ended. Each event is sent at most once per method, or per tool and outcome, while korTTY runs; the number of calls goes into the periodic usage summary.
a Control API method is used for the first time in this run
the method name, such as KTPH000, and the kind of client: KTPH001 for KTPH002, KTPH003 for an MCP client, KTPH004 for any other program
an MCP client's call ends in a way not yet reported in this run

the tool (KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004, KTPH005, KTPH006, KTPH007, or KTPH008) and the outcome: KTPH009, KTPH010 (switched off, not allowed or not possible in this pane), KTPH011 (you said no, or korTTY could not ask), KTPH012 (nobody answered in time, or a wait ran out) or KTPH013 (any other error)
The client's name, pane ids, tool arguments, the text read or typed and the answers you gave are never sent.

When an SFTP Manager tab opens, one event says whether it shares a terminal's session. When an upload or download in the SFTP Manager finishes, one event says how it went. File counts are rounded down to 0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 50, 100 or 1000. When korTTY stops watching a file you edited in an external editor (also as root), one event says how the edit ended; upload counts are rounded down to 0, 1, 2, 5, 10 or 50.
whether it uses a terminal pane's SSH session or a login of its own
an upload or download batch (one button press or one drop) is finished
KTPH000 or KTPH001, the rounded number of files, whether it ended KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004 or KTPH005, whether a file continued a partial file, and how many files were copied at once
korTTY stops watching a file opened with KTPH000Edit in External EditorKTPH001 or KTPH002Edit as Root (sudo)...KTPH003
KTPH000 or KTPH001, whether it ended KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004, KTPH005 or KTPH006, and the rounded number of uploads
File and folder names, paths, server names, editor commands, sudo passwords and file sizes are never sent.
When the JobScheduler shows a desktop notification for a job run or sends one to a webhook target, one event says how it went.
a run notification is shown on the desktop, or delivered, refused or blocked for one webhook target
KTPH000 or KTPH001, the payload format (KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004 or KTPH005), whether it ended KTPH006, KTPH007 or KTPH008, and the number of delivery attempts (0 to 3)
Job and target names, webhook URLs and hosts, run status texts and anything of the run's output are never sent. A test sent with KTPH000Send testKTPH001 is not counted.
korTTY never transmits any of the following:
Hostnames, IP addresses, usernames, or connection names and addresses
File names, paths, or directory contents
Snippet content, terminal output, or AI prompt and chat text
Passwords, SSH keys, GPG keys, or API keys
Error messages (only the type of error and the korTTY class where it occurred)

Usage statistics are processed by KTPH001KTPH002AptabaseKTPH003KTPH004, an open-source, privacy-first analytics service. korTTY uses Aptabase's KTPH005EU regionKTPH006 (KTPH000), so the data is processed on servers located in the European Union in compliance with the KTPH007GDPRKTPH008. See the KTPH009Aptabase privacy policyKTPH010 for details.

If no connection is available, events are cached locally in KTPH000 and sent later — including after a restart — so a temporary lack of connectivity does not lose or block anything. This offline cache holds only the same anonymous events; it is discarded if you opt out, and events older than three days are dropped.
The goal is to make korTTY better with real, anonymous evidence instead of guesswork:
KTPH000Prioritize featuresKTPH001 that people actually use, and retire ones that nobody does.
KTPH000Find crashes and frequent errorsKTPH001 so they can be fixed in the next release.
KTPH000Measure whether releases improve stabilityKTPH001 over time.
KTPH000First launch:KTPH001 the setup dialog for the master password includes the pre-selected checkbox and this information; clearing it before you click KTPH002SetupKTPH003 declines.
KTPH000Any time:KTPH001 open KTPH002Settings → PrivacyKTPH003 to enable or disable collection. The same page links back to this chapter.
KTPH000Turning it offKTPH001 stops all collection immediately and discards data that has not yet been sent.

Your decision and the date it was made are stored locally in KTPH000 (see KTPH001Configuration filesKTPH002) as a record of consent. If a future korTTY version changes what is collected, you will be asked again so your choice always reflects the current scope.
